state: Support case summary, 17 July 2026. Our cloud backup service had one outage in July, on 14 July from 09:20 to 13:05 UTC; there were no other outages that month. The service agreement promises 99.9% uptime per calendar month, measured over every hour of the month. If monthly uptime is below 99.9% but at least 99.0%, the customer gets a credit of 10% of that month's fee; below 99.0%, the credit is 25%. Credits must be claimed within 30 days of the incident. Aldermoor Dental (plan fee 240.00 per month) emailed on 16 July asking for a 50% refund for July, saying they "lost a day of patient records". Our logs show that their local backup agent queued all changes during the outage and finished uploading them by 13:40 UTC the same day, with no files missing. The practice manager says the outage meant staff could not restore an old file that morning and had to phone a patient back later.

q1.instructions: Where does the service's July uptime fall against the agreement's bands?
